name: round-history
title: Round history
description: A bounded record of rounds and who won what in each, with voided rounds, per-player totals, and a portable ndjson export. Server, Apple and Android.

facilities.description: Append rounds, keep the newest N, query and export them

text.purpose: Players want to see how the last rounds went. This component keeps a list of rounds, each `{no, level, winners: [{playerId, amount}], voided}`, bounded to the newest `maxRounds` (the oldest fall off). A cancelled round is recorded as voided with no winners. It answers who won how much over the rounds held, finds a round by number, and exports and imports the list as ndjson with a checksum per line. It knows nothing about the game: `level` is simply the stage the round was played at. A game that records its own fields beside the result (the pot, the showdown kind) pushes a plain object and gets the same object back from `list`.
text.userInputs: The installer collects one setting: `maxRounds`, how many rounds to keep (whole number, at least 1; default 50, as in the recipe).
text.integration: The server appends an entry when a round ends (the recipe does this where a hand is settled and where a hand is cancelled) and puts `history.rounds` in the view it sends. Round numbers must rise within one history, so a new game starts a new history with `clearHistory`. Apple and Android clients use `HistoryEntry` to read the list from the view and `RoundHistory` to keep a bounded copy; the Apple type is `Decodable` like the recipe's, the Kotlin classes are plain data classes to which `@Serializable` is added where the wire format is decoded. `turn-engine` requires this interface. The engine form is `create()`, `push(history, {no, level, voided, ...game fields})` and `list(history)` (oldest first); `createHistoryApi({maxRounds})` binds the setting. Game fields are kept in `extra` and must be plain JSON; Apple and Android read the four typed fields and ignore `extra`.
text.infrastructure: No deployed service and no accounts. The history is plain data kept in the game state; export and import move it between hosts.
text.verification: `tests/web.test.ts` (required-local) checks bounds, validation, rising round numbers, voided rounds, totals, queries, ndjson round trip with a tampered line rejected, the engine form (create, push, list with game fields, rising numbers, plain-JSON check, copies, export and import with game fields) and the consumer example. `tests/native.py apple` compiles `RoundHistory.swift` with swiftc, decodes `tests/fixtures/rounds.json` as JSON and checks the bound and totals (run and passed on this machine). `tests/native.py android` does the same with kotlinc; kotlinc is not installed here, so it was written but not run.
text.scenarios: A hold'em tournament shows the last 50 hands. A short party game keeps 10 rounds. A support engineer exports the history of a disputed game. A new game clears the list.
text.updates: Patch updates replace the files only. The ndjson record layout is in `interfaces/round.schema.json` and `migration.json`. After removal, exported files are described by the schema.

agentInstructions: Select this component for any game that shows past rounds. Set `maxRounds` from the recipe (hold'em: 50). Connect the provided `round-history` to the turn engine. Include the Apple and Android files only when those client targets are selected.
developerInstructions: Keep the `History` in the game state and replace it with each function's result. Append once per finished or cancelled round, with a rising `no`. Do not store card detail here; the history is a result log. No accounts or keys.

suitability.notes: Pure library; no provider limits apply. 50 rounds is a few kilobytes.
